title: CraftConfig
description:
A world's full craft config — the aggregate the engine loads as data and
[`apply`]s over the shipped doctrine packs (design §1.2, §2.4).

Only [`enabled_packs`](Self::enabled_packs), [`overlays`](Self::overlays), and
[`world_principles`](Self::world_principles) bear on the composed principle
corpus; the remaining fields are season/outline policy consumed by the
relevant check entry points (design §2.3).

enabled_packs.description: The doctrine packs this world turns on.

factory_namespaces.description: The factory-battery namespaces this world runs prose checks through.

overlays.description: The overlays riding on shipped generic principles.

precedence_tier.description: The precedence tier (the pillar mechanism, world-populated).

text_rules.description: Caller-owned lexical checks over outline slots.

world_principles.description: The config-only principle rows (incl. the pillars).

oneOf.description: A deterministic kernel rule (the reference cannot dangle — closed enum).
A deterministic check that stays factory-side (spec §6), recorded not run.

symbol.description: The check symbol within that battery.

oneOf.description:
A judge dimension: consumes a stored attestation of this question kind and
reports grade [`Grade::Attested`].
Declaration-only: no check, surfaced by brief/phase queries.

Disposition.description: What a narrator-framing choice earns: an error, a warning, or nothing.

oneOf.description: The framing is forbidden — an error finding.
The framing is discouraged — a warn finding.
The framing is permitted — no finding.

FactoryNs.description:
A caller-declared factory-side check namespace (spec §6: prose checks stay
factory-invoked).

This is an open identifier rather than an engine-owned enum: projects may
register any factory namespace and [`super::worldcfg::validate`] checks every
factory binding against that registry.

Family.description: A doctrine family — the axis a principle speaks to.

oneOf.description: Plot: promises, causality, try/fail, arc shape.
Character: sliders, interiority, voice.
World: material grounding, magic pedagogy, allegory.
Prose: sentence craft, abstraction, said-ratio.
Serial: open loops, micro-pacing, installment discipline.
Audio: narrator/SFX load, aural distinctness, performability.
Pillar: a project-specific principle that overrides generic advice.

FindingRuleCfg.description:
The citation (+ optional severity override) a finding code carries — the loadable
form of [`super::config::FindingRule`] (design §3 item 4).

citations.description: The citations attached to the finding, in order.

code.description: The dotted finding code this rule governs.

severity.description: An optional severity override; `None` keeps the code's intrinsic severity.

KernelRule.description:
The **closed** set of deterministic kernel rules a principle may bind.

A `checkable: deterministic` principle over kernel objects names its rule here,
so a reference to a rule that does not exist is a compile error — the legacy
`check_ref_resolves` test, lifted into the type system. The outline entry
points are the `CRAFT-1` batteries; the season rules are `CRAFT-2`'s join
engine ([`super::season`]), and the two layers share this one rule namespace.

oneOf.description: The `CRAFT-1` per-episode structural battery ([`super::season::check_episode`]).
The `CRAFT-1` season-scope battery ([`super::season::check_season`]).
Accomplishment-earned: a major beat needs a prior same-thread failure.
The climax refinement: a climax-class beat needs two prior failures.
A thread that lands its unqualified win may not re-open.
Competence-consistency: an unearned major win by an under-competent hand.
The arc-flat generalization of the flat-slider check, at season scope.
Kishōtenketsu fair-play: a turn's reframing fact must be on the ledger early.
A mystery promise untouched for K episodes is starved.
Cold-open discipline: open a loop, cast ≤ 2, no deep-time in act 1.
New named speakers per episode within a band and a season budget.
Two names below the aural-distinctness floor may not share a scene.
Promise open/close density banded by season position.
A kishōtenketsu episode places its *ten* in-band, not as a clash resolution.
No run of N high-orientation-load episodes.

MaterialCategoryCfg.description:
One material-planning category and whether a worldbuilding review requires it —
loadable form of [`super::config::MaterialCategory`] (design §3 item 7).

required.description: Whether a material-worldbuilding review requires it.

MaterialCategoryId.description: An open caller-owned material-planning category identifier.

oneOf.description: The principle applies to the mission unchanged.
The principle applies with a caveat; the caveat is required.

note.description: Why the generic principle needs adapting to the mission.

oneOf.description:
A generic principle conflicts with a pillar or with canon; the resolution
(the mission-side ruling) is required (spec §5).

note.description: The conflict between the received principle and the mission.

resolution.description: The mission-side ruling that resolves it — where the pillar wins.

NarratorMode.description: The narrator framing of an audio packet.

oneOf.description: No narrator at all.
A windowpane narrator — transparent orientation, no personality.
A frame narrator.
A tale-host narrator (a host-narrator ban is world policy).

NarratorModeRuleCfg.description:
The disposition a single narrator mode earns — loadable form of
[`super::config::NarratorModeRule`] (design §3 item 5).

mode.description: The narrator mode this rule governs.

NarratorPolicyCfg.description: The narrator-framing policy — loadable form of [`super::config::NarratorPolicy`].

direct_address.description: The disposition a direct-audience-address plan earns.

mode_rules.description: Per-mode dispositions; modes absent here are [`Disposition::Allowed`].

OutlineThresholdsCfg.description:
The world's outline scalars + turn slot — the loadable companion to
[`super::season::EpisodePolicy`]'s scalars and [`super::config::ArcShapeCatalog`]
(design §3 items 2, 8).

turn_slot.description: Which kishōtenketsu slot the battle-scan reads as the turn.

Phase.description: A production phase a principle bears on.

oneOf.description: The outline phase.
The lore-decision phase.
The generation phase.
The revision phase.

PrecedenceTier.description:
The world's precedence tier — the generic pillar mechanism, world-populated.
The tier that wins a conflict plus the standing-rule text.

PrincipleOverlay.description:
A world ruling that rides on a shipped [`DoctrinePrinciple`] by id — the config
half of a generic-plus-overlay principle (design §1.2).

It carries exactly what the shipped record cannot: the world's mission filter,
its provenance citations, the concrete runtime binding (the factory battery or
judge dimension the generic record only typed as a *kind*), the pillar-tier
promotion, and — when the world's authored wording diverges from the shipped
generic body — a statement/source override.

binding.description:
The concrete runtime binding — the factory battery / judge dimension / kernel
rule the composed principle checks by.

citations.description: The provenance citations (`D-nnnn` / canon anchors) that justify the ruling.

in_precedence_tier.description:
Promote this generic principle into the world's precedence tier (→
[`Family::Pillar`]).

mission_filter.description: How the mission filters the received principle (default [`MissionFilter::Pass`]).

param_overrides.description:
Overrides for the shipped record's generic default parameters (metadata; the
runtime [`Principle`] record carries no parameters).

principle_id.description: The shipped principle this overlay rides on; must resolve to an enabled pack.

source.description:
A world-specific source/citation string that overrides the shipped source
(absent when unchanged).

statement.description:
A world-specific statement that overrides the shipped generic wording (absent
when the shipped statement already reads world-agnostic and unchanged).

ProvenanceCfg.description:
The reference-format patterns provenance guards accept — loadable form of
[`super::config::ProvenanceFormats`] (design §3 item 6).

canon_digits.description: The exact digit count following the canon prefix.

research_id_digits.description: The exact digit count following the research-id prefix.

research_path_digits.description: The digit count following the research-doc path prefix.

research_url_schemes.description: Accepted research-URL scheme prefixes, tried in order.

Scalar.description:
A generic default parameter value carried by a shipped [`DoctrinePrinciple`] —
a world may override it in its craft config (design §1.1). Deliberately small:
the tunables in the corpus are counts, ratios, flags, and short labels
(e.g. `said_tag_ratio = 0.85`, `cast_per_scene = 4`, `tryfail_count = 3`).

Severity.description: How much a [`WorldFinding`] must be attended to.

oneOf.description:
A violation: the world (or a draft) contradicts canon or asserts what it
may not.
A defect worth a look that does not, on its own, break canon.

TextMatchRuleCfg.description: A caller-defined lexical finding over one outline slot.

Thresholds.description:
The calibratable policy thresholds the season rules read (spec §4) — every
numeric band, one place, D-citable. Substituting a table is a data diff citing
a ruling, never a code change. [`DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS`] ships uncalibrated, so the
band rules ride at [`Severity::Warn`].

Carries `f64` bands, so it is `PartialEq` but not `Eq`.

audio_high_run.description: No run of this many consecutive high-orientation-load episodes.

calibrated.description:
Whether these thresholds are calibrated against the season-1 corpus. Ships
`false`; band findings ride at warn until it is `true` (spec §4).

cast_introduction_band.description: New named speakers per episode should sit within this inclusive band.

climax_prior_failures.description: A climax-class accomplishment needs at least this many (a warn below it).

cold_open_cast_ceiling.description: A cold open may carry at most this many speaking voices.

competence_floor.description:
Below this competence, a major unassisted win needs an intervening growth
or price beat.

major_prior_failures.description:
A `>= major` accomplishment needs at least this many prior same-thread
failures (an error below it — the worked join).

mystery_starved_gap.description: An open mystery untouched for this many consecutive episodes is starved.

reveal_lead_episodes.description:
A turn's reframing fact must sit on the listener ledger at least this many
episodes before the turn.

season_cast_budget.description: The season named-cast budget, when set (total introductions ceiling).

ten_position_band.description: A kishōtenketsu *ten* should land within this inclusive fraction band.

TokenPairCfg.description: One adjacent-token pattern in a configured lexical rule.

TurnSlot.description:
Which kishōtenketsu slot names the *turn* the outline battle-scan reads. The
`ki`/`shō`/`ten`/`ketsu` fields stay on the outline (kishōtenketsu is a named
framework, not world content); the catalog drives only *which* slot is scanned.

oneOf.description: The opening image.
The development.
The turn.
The resolution.

WorldPrinciple.description:
A config-only principle — a world row with no shipped generic kernel (design
§1.2). It converts straight to a runtime [`Principle`]; its
[`family`](Self::family) may be [`Family::Pillar`].

citations.description: The provenance citations that justify the row.

family.description: The family (may be [`Family::Pillar`] — the world's precedence tier).

finding_codes.description: Exact kernel finding codes governed by this principle.

parameters.description: Parameters consumed by this principle's binding.

phases.description: The production phases it bears on.

source.description: The provenance — a canon anchor or `D-nnnn` ruling.

statement.description: The principle, stated in the world's own terms (world content allowed).
